summary: The bill amends the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act to require OMB to create a Congress-only real-time hyperlink on the federal awards website that includes payment details for individual recipients and federal employees.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act to give Members of Congress real-time access to detailed federal award and payment data (including to individuals and employees). This directly enhances spending oversight and transparency, which is intended to support identification and reduction of wasteful expenditures. It therefore has a moderate positive alignment with reducing government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, coverage, or regulation.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration policy or border enforcement.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions that alter military or defense spending levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.

The bill expands congressional access to data on federal assistance payments to individuals, which could indirectly support oversight of safety-net programs, but it does not change eligibility, funding, or benefit levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to education funding or school policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.

By improving real-time transparency on federal outlays, the bill supports congressional efforts to identify and curb deficit-increasing spending, giving it a tangential positive alignment with debt-reduction priorities.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill contains no provisions that change foreign aid levels or policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill expands congressional access to data on federal payments to individuals and employees but does not impose new privacy regulations or oversight on technology companies.
The bill contains no provisions related to labor unions or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
